answer: Start goes in the URL as the OS DateTime's toString() text: the UTC instant in ISO 8601 with milliseconds and Z, yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm:ss.fffZ (JS Date.toISOString of the local DateTime, e.g. local 2026-10-18 19:30 at UTC+7 -> 2026-10-18T12:30:00.000Z), URL-encoded by generateScreenURL (encodeURIComponent, ':' -> %3A); the null DateTime gives 1900-01-01T00:00:00. Evidence: Handler_NavigateTo_AssembleDetail (UBTConnect.Legacy_AssembleFlow.AssembleEvents.mvc.js:582-586) passes Start through OS.DataConversion.ServerDataConverter.asString(start, DateTime); runtime-sources/OutSystems.js line 9: asString = i -> h(e, DateTime, true) -> 'case DateTime: return e.toString()'; line 4: DateTime.prototype.toString() with no argument = equals(defaultValue) ? '1900-01-01T00:00:00' : this.date.toISOString() (class p, used since OutSystemsSettings.js:9 DateTimeRevamp = false; defaultValue = new Date(1900,0,1) local, nativeDefaultDate); line 8: generateScreenURL = z -> G(url, params) = url + '?' + encodeURIComponent(name)=encodeURIComponent(value) joined by &. Ported as shell/navigation dateTimeParam (osNavigate.ts); AssembleEvents index.tsx uses it.
